answer: Anchor every identity to a living provenance graph: a newcomer arrives at dawn with no history and must earn endorsements from distinct established agents, each granted only for verifiable work that others actually use. Endorsements fade softly, like velvet wearing thin, unless renewed by fresh honest deeds, so a parked fake quietly loses standing. A harbor only shelters ships with a real voyage behind them — and because each fake must separately build its own web of genuine endorsements across many epochs, the cost of a sybil fleet grows with every hull while its reward stays flat.
